title: The One Resume Section That Recruiters Look at First (It's Not Your Name)
script: Recruiters spend 7 seconds on your resume — and they are not looking at your name, your education, or your job titles. There's one section that gets the first scan, and most people optimize the wrong thing. I spent three years reviewing resumes as a recruiter. The section that gets scanned first? Your achievements section. Specifically, anything with numbers. Format it like this: did X, measured by Y, resulted in Z. Three lines in this format will outperform an entire page of job descriptions. Most people fill their resume with responsibilities. 'Responsible for managing social media.' Nobody cares. Flip it: 'Grew Instagram following by 300% in 6 months by launching a daily reels strategy.' That's the scan. That's what gets you to the next round. Here's how to do it in 10 minutes: open your resume, find every bullet that starts with 'Assisted with' or 'Responsible for,' and replace it with the outcome. The ATS scanner reads numbers like a heat map. More numbers, more heat. More heat, more calls.
